title: Ridgeline Warranty Coverage Rate Card Clause: Billable Labor Hours and the Labor Charge
content:
**Clause.** The method hours of a Warranty Coverage technician visit are the hours on site with the labor minimum applied: a visit shorter than the labor minimum is billed for the minimum, and any time beyond the minimum is rounded up to the plan's billing increment. The labor minimum is the plan's minimum billable labor per visit. The billable labor hours of a visit start from its method hours and are booked on the labor charge to one decimal place, and the labor charge is the billable labor hours times the warranty plan's hourly labor rate.

**Order of working.** The method hours are raised by the lead-safe allowance and the sum is multiplied by the labor crew rate, giving the billable labor hours, which are booked on the labor charge to one decimal place; the plan's hourly labor rate is reduced by the labor program discount; the billable labor hours are multiplied by that rate and then by the labor day rate; and the result is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end, an amount exactly halfway between two cents going to the higher cent. The lead-safe allowance and the labor program discount are zero, and the labor crew rate and the labor day rate are one.

The hourly labor rate, the minimum billable labor and the billing increment are the figures of the plan's field service rate card. The visit priced is the latest technician visit recorded on the claim, with its hours on site.

## Method hours — worked (hypothetical: minimum 1.0 hour, increment 0.5 hour, rate 100.00)

| Hours on site | Method hours | Labor charge |
|---|---|---|
| 0.6 | 1.0 (the minimum) | 100.00 |
| 1.0 | 1.0 | 100.00 |
| 1.2 | 1.5 (0.2 beyond the minimum rounds up to one increment) | 150.00 |
| 1.5 | 1.5 | 150.00 |
| 2.1 | 2.5 | 250.00 |

The time beyond the minimum is what is rounded up, so 1.2 hours become the minimum plus one increment, 1.5 hours.

## Rounding

Billable hours are booked to one decimal place; the charge is rounded once, to the cent, after the last multiplication.
